dataflow.summary: Attacker Host header -> disabled Vite Host-validation middleware -> development source serving.

impact.why: Workspace source or unreleased mockups may be read; no secrets or host execution established.

likelihood.why: Requires developer interaction and a permissive browser/network path.

reachability.summary: Requires a running development server and successful browser/network rebinding; no privileged account required.

attackPath.summary: A developer runs either HTTP development server and visits a malicious origin. If DNS rebinding reaches that server, the attacker's hostname is accepted and same-origin script can read development-served source.

codeEvidence.explanation: An attacker-controlled Host value is accepted by the all-interface HTTP development server; filesystem strict mode limits file scope but does not validate the browser origin.
codeEvidence.label: Public-site development server disables host checks

codeEvidence.explanation: The mockup development server also accepts arbitrary Host values and can serve unreleased source under a rebound attacker origin.
codeEvidence.label: Mockup server disables the same control

confidence.rationale: Both repository configs explicitly set allowedHosts:true; installed Vite source confirms this bypasses host validation. Runtime exploitation was not attempted.

preventiveControls: Keep development servers private and separate from the public static production server.
findings.remediation: Restore Vite Host validation in both development configs, default to loopback binding, and explicitly allow only controlled development hostnames when remote previews are required.
remediationTests: With each dev config, an unrecognized Host header returns 403 while localhost and explicitly configured development hosts still work.
Verify remote preview requirements with a narrow controlled hostname allowlist; do not use allowedHosts:true.

rootCause.summary: Both development entry points bind to all interfaces and set allowedHosts to true. Vite consumes that boolean by omitting host-validation middleware, so requests bearing an attacker-controlled hostname can reach development source serving. Filesystem strict mode limits reachable files but does not restore origin validation.

severity.rationale: Conditional developer-only source disclosure requires a running HTTP development server and successful browser/network rebinding. No production secret access or code execution established.

findings.summary: Opening a malicious website while a P1 development server is running can expose workspace source through DNS rebinding when the browser and network permit it. Both development configs disable Vite's Host-header protection.
findings.title: Development servers accept arbitrary Host headers

limitations: Browser local-network protections, DNS behavior, developer browsing and server reachability govern exploitability.
The production preview serves built public files; this finding concerns development source confidentiality.
validation.summary: Inspected both complete Vite configs and installed Vite 7.3.3 config.js:25616; middleware installation is guarded by allowedHosts !== true. Confirmed development scripts invoke Vite with these configs. No application or exploit was run.
